subject: Long/short context budgeting & decision plan
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightcart.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Long/short context budgeting & decision plan

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and where I think we should focus before we put pricing on paper.

Call highlights
- BrightCart use case: personalized product descriptions + multi-turn assistant for seller help. Primary production surface is user-facing generate API called from the web app.
- Current rough volume: you estimated ~850k user-facing calls/month + ~150k internal batch/analytics calls = ~1.0M calls/month (you confirmed in the call).
- Token profile (you provided example sample; asked me to validate): average prompt length ~1,100 tokens; average completion ~1,900 tokens.
- Context needs: majority of requests are short or medium context, but a non-trivial tail requires long context (historical thread + catalog slice). You mentioned 8k for day-to-day, occasional 32k for merchant threads, and rare archival lookups up to 128k.

What I captured (please correct if any number is off)
- Avg prompt tokens: 1,100
- Avg completion tokens: 1,900
- Avg tokens / call: 3,000
- Distribution: ~78% requests fit within 8k, ~17% require 32k, ~5% require 128k
- Monthly calls: 1,000,000 -> monthly tokens = ~3,000,000,000 (3,000M)

Why this matters for pricing
- Model choice + context length materially changes per-token cost (8k vs 32k vs 128k memory + throughput implications).
- Batching, KV/prefix caching, and truncation strategies can reduce effective completion tokens and lower unit cost.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Could you attach the sample CSV you referenced in the call (timestamps, request type, prompt_len, completion_len) — I'll validate the distribution and run a quick cost sensitivity.
2) What's the internal budget range you're comfortable with for total monthly inference spend (range is fine, e.g., $150k–$300k / $300k–$600k / $600k+). This helps me recommend Hosted vs Dedicated pricing.
3) If possible, pencil a 45-min technical deep-dive next week with one of our inference engineers so we can map caching/batching opportunities.

I'll follow up with a ballpark unit-econ scenario once I get the CSV. Attached is our pricing matrix (v2) and a short checklist of data we prefer for profiling.

Attachments: brightcart_usage_sample.csv (placeholder), redwood_pricing_matrix_v2.pdf

Thanks —
Irene Choi

Thanks, Irene — great summary. A few corrections/clarifications inline: 

> - Avg prompt tokens: 1,100
> - Avg completion tokens: 1,900
> - Avg tokens / call: 3,000

Those averages look right for the user-facing surface. For internal batch jobs the completion side is heavier (we get long catalogs merged into a single generation) so those calls push the mean up slightly, but the numbers you have are fine for projection.

On distribution: the %s you captured are accurate for production traffic today — 78/17/5 is a solid approximation. The 128k calls are rare (merchant archival lookups) and mostly scheduled.

Budget range: leadership has put a preliminary monthly target of $300k–$450k for inference. We're focused on predictable unit economics vs absolute lowest possible price. We may consider a dedicated commitment if the guaranteed throughput + lower unit price is compelling and contractually predictable.

CSV: attaching the sample export from our infra (includes request_type, session_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, timestamp). Let me know if you want a larger extract.

Next: book the deep-dive — Tue/Thu next week mornings PT work well.

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>

Elena — received, thanks for the CSV (attached to this thread). I ran a quick sensitivity using the sample and sketched three concise scenarios so we can align to BrightCart's budget/risk tolerance. I kept this high-level so we can iterate in the technical deep-dive.

Assumptions (from sample + call)
- Monthly calls: 1,000,000
- Avg tokens/call: 3,000 (1,100 prompt / 1,900 completion)
- Monthly tokens: 3,000M (3,000 x 1M calls)
- Distribution: 78% 8k, 17% 32k, 5% 128k (affects memory & model selection but tokens counted consistently)

Scenario A — Hosted (no commitment)- List unit cost assumption (example): $/1M tokens = $900
- Estimated monthly spend = 3,000 x $900 = $2,700,000
- Pros: quickest to start, no infra commitments.
- Cons: higher unit cost, less predictability at scale.

Scenario B — Committed Dedicated (12-mo)- Negotiated unit $/1M tokens = $450 (example for committed capacity & preferred routing)
- Estimated monthly spend = 3,000 x $450 = $1,350,000
- Pros: predictable unit economics, SLA-backed latency, capacity isolation.
- Cons: commitment required; procurement lead time.

Scenario C — Hybrid (Hosted + Dedicated routing + caching)- Assume 60% of traffic on Dedicated (lower unit $/1M = $400), 40% on Hosted (burst/rare 128k). Effective blended $/1M ≈ $640
- Estimated monthly spend ≈ 3,000 x $640 = $1,920,000
- Pros: preserves burstability for rare 128k jobs; reduces overall spend vs pure Hosted.

Levers to reduce spend (practical items we can target in the technical deep-dive)- Prefix/KV caching for repeated product descriptions (can cut prompt tokens by 20–60% for repetitive content).- Aggressive completion truncation for non-critical assistant replies (drop 10–25% tail).- Quantized model variants for high-volume short-context calls (material per-token CPU/GPU cost reduction).- Routing by policy: route 8k traffic to cheaper model variants; reserve expensive context models for 128k workflows only.

My recommendation for the next meeting
1) Technical deep-dive with an inference engineer + solutions architect to map what can be pushed into caching and quantify savings (45 min).
2) If BrightCart is comfortable with the ~$300k–$450k monthly target, we should scope a Dedicated 12-month pilot quote (I'll involve commercial). If the target is lower, we can prioritize caching + model-mix to bring effective unit economics down before a full commit.

I've attached the quick sensitivity spreadsheet (redwood_pricing_matrix_v2.pdf) and the cleaned sample CSV you sent. Karthik — looping you in so commercial can help shape the pilot commit and procurement timeline.

Thanks —
Irene
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
